When `print` tries to write those characters to the Windows console, it attempts to encode them using the default code page (cp1252), which fails and likely raises a UnicodeEncodeError, causing the script to abort or truncate output.

A straightforward fix is to ensure that the string we print contains only characters that can be encoded in cp1252. One way is to re‑encode the cleaned text to ASCII, replacing any non‑ASCII characters with a placeholder (e.g., `?`). This can be done with `text.encode("ascii", errors="replace").decode("ascii")`. By inserting this step after the ANSI stripping, we guarantee that the subsequent `print` calls will not raise encoding errors.
